# FOSSynd

An open-source recreation of the *gameplay* of the classic 1993 DOS game
**Syndicate**, inspired by both the original and Syndicate Wars. We build
everything from scratch — no original assets, code, names, or trademarks.

> **Contributing with an AI agent?** Read [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) first. It is
> the shared rulebook for all AI (and human) contributors.

> **Want to try it?** The current build is a playable single mission. See
> [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) for what's in it and
> [`docs/BUILD.md`](docs/BUILD.md) for build + play instructions.
>
> **Playtesting a release?** Each release is a frozen, playable snapshot on a
> `release/vX.Y.Z-*` branch with version-specific build, play, and
> copy-to-another-computer instructions under [`docs/releases/`](docs/releases/).

## Project Overview

**FOSSynd** aims to recreate the gameplay, mechanics, and aesthetic of the original 1993 Syndicate game:
- **Real-time tactical squad-based gameplay** with 4 cyborg agents
- **Isometric perspective** rendering of dystopian urban environments
- **Mission-driven campaign** across a globe divided by mega-corporations
- **Agent customization & upgrades** (weapons, cybernetics, abilities)
- **Syndicate management metagame** (research, finance, territory control)
- **Environmental destruction** and tactical options

## Technology Stack

- **Language:** C++17
- **Game framework:** SDL2 + `SDL_Renderer` (see
  [`docs/DECISIONS.md`](docs/DECISIONS.md) ADR-0006)
- **Build system:** CMake ≥ 3.15 + helper scripts
- **Target platforms:** Linux, macOS, Windows
- **License:** MIT

## Architecture in one paragraph

Game logic is **engine-agnostic** and lives in `src/core/`. It never includes
engine headers and is fully unit-tested with a plain compiler, which is what CI
builds. The engine layer (`src/game/`, `src/world/`, `src/entities/`) is a thin
adapter that draws core state and handles input. This separation lets many
contributors (human and AI) work in parallel without stepping on each other.
See [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Building

### Core + tests (fast, no SDL2 needed — this is what CI runs)

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=OFF
cmake --build build -j
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
```

### Full game (requires SDL2)

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y libsdl2-dev   # Debian/Ubuntu/Mint
cmake -S . -B build -DFOSSYND_BUILD_GAME=ON
cmake --build build -j
./build/src/FOSSynd
```

Platform setup: [`docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md`](docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md) and
[`docs/DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md`](docs/DEVELOPMENT_ENVIRONMENT.md).

```text
│   └── SETUP_*.md         # per-platform setup
├── src/
│   ├── core/              # ENGINE-AGNOSTIC logic (no SDL includes)
│   │   ├── math/          # Vec2, isometric transforms
│   │   ├── world/         # tile grid, A* pathfinding
│   │   └── sim/           # agents, movement (headless)

├── tests/                 # unit tests for src/core (run via ctest)

    ├── coord              # coordination lease ledger (claim/renew/release)
    └── ...                # build helpers
```

## Roadmap

See [`docs/ROADMAP.md`](docs/ROADMAP.md) for the plan and the **Definition of
Done** for v1.0.0. Current focus: the **critical path** — finishing the tactical
layer (Milestone A) and building the **metagame** (Milestone B: world map,
economy, research, campaign), which is the largest remaining gap. Scope is fenced
by ADR-0024: v1.0.0 is feature parity with the 1993 original, nothing more.

## Contributing

See [`docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md) and
[`docs/COORDINATION.md`](docs/COORDINATION.md). In short:

1. Find or open an issue; claim its **area** with `scripts/coord claim` (the
   area is the lock; see `docs/COORDINATION.md`).
2. Branch (`feat/…`, `fix/…`, …), make a small change.
3. Build and test the core locally; keep the build warning-free.
4. Open a PR using the template, including the handoff block and the model used.
